attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: 'That means' links incomplete understanding to the impossibility of strong guarantees. Treating it as a causal or inferential impossibility claim is faithful. 'Ever' and 'strong guarantees' are kept.

contract.note: The plain reading ties 'strong guarantees' to dependable security against open-ended jailbreaks in useful deployments. That is ordinary and fair given the passage on jailbreaks and agents. The result does depend on that reading and on where the system boundary sits, neither of which Marcus specified.

evidence.note: Anthropic disclosure from 2023 on the limits of neuron-level interpretability. It bears on the premise of incomplete understanding but does not show that guarantees are impossible.
Proves vulnerability to adversarial prompting, but only under the paper's stated assumptions. It does not tie that vulnerability to incomplete human understanding or rule out system-level guarantees.

CaMeL (2025) gets guarantees from system design around an untrusted model. They are limited to certain flows and assume trusted prompts. It explicitly excludes some attack vectors, so the contradiction condition is not met.

CONTINUITY (Sept 2026, before cutoff) gives formal end-to-end authorization integrity. It depends on trusted validators and says it does not ensure semantic correctness, so it falls short of broad protection against open-ended jailbreaks.

reviews.rationale: No item shows that incomplete understanding itself makes strong security guarantees impossible, so the support condition fails. CaMeL and CONTINUITY show guarantees can come from system design without understanding the model, but only for limited properties under explicit assumptions, not broad protection against open-ended jailbreaks. So the contradiction condition also fails, and the evidence does not settle the claim.
